newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco rail union wage rise wins approval.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco rail union wage rise wins approval.

text.p: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors on Monday approved a union contract that was projected to cost the city more than $21 million.

The board unanimously voted to approve the Municipal Railway union contract, which would give drivers a 4.7 percent wage increase. The contract was expected to be taken up by the board again next Monday for a second and final vote.
The wage increase was projected to cost San Francisco about $4.7 million for fiscal year 1996-1997, according to Harvey Rose, budget analyst to the Board of Supervisors.

The wage and benefits package would cost San Francisco at least $21.5 million over the next three fiscal years, Rose said. No cost estimates have been prepared for the fourth fiscal year under the contract.
